title: Determine both even-width five-qubit Clifford denominator growth rates
body:
At every even tensor width $f\ge16$, the five-qubit Clifford Gram operator has explicit attained spectral endpoints. For the canonical decoder let $D_f$ be its least positive odd denominator over the Gaussian dyadics. The two even subsequences obey

- $\log_2D_f=295(f-2)+O(1)$ for $f\equiv0\pmod4$.
- $\log_2D_f=190(f-2)+O(1)$ for $f\equiv2\pmod4$.

The joint spectral polynomial LCMs have degrees 592 and 381, with zero-root multiplicities two and one respectively. Computing the full inverse projector coefficients gives exact canonical denominators of **727, 997, 2,073 and 1,829 bits** at widths 16, 18, 20 and 22. The proof keeps the canonical denominator distinct from the denominator attainable by a norm-optimal inverse.

The nonzero-vector stabilizer calculation uses its affine radical. A native permutation-group calculation and an independent lower-rank recursion agree on all 322 irreducible rows and 143 distinct spectral polynomials for this stabilizer. An additional direct binary-matrix calculation checks 2,906 invariant-character Fourier identities on every small Levi element through rank three. The endpoint certificates include exact polynomial inequalities for the infinite tails as well as the finite low widths.

This completes both even residue classes following #7806, #7810 and the odd-width arithmetic in #7812. It uses the sector framework of alephnan, the conditioning and arithmetic of Ali Romman and the GAP/CTblLib character tables credited in the package. It supplies decoder quantities; the selected conditional multiplication exponent remains 0.00363005817.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.
